slides.0.title: AOCs: three sets of rules
slides.0.subtitle: The most detailed part of Morocco's rules
slides.1.title: Rules for every AOC (1998)
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Picking and cellars
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Grapes go in perforated crates, cellars need cooling and stainless steel or equivalent, and continuous presses and screw conveyors are banned
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The threshold at the cellar door
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Each lot must reach at least 187 g/L sugar, and concentration is not allowed. In exceptionally poor years there are derogations, and whites may drop to 178 g/L
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Enrichment only in very poor years
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The minister may allow up to 1% vol of enrichment with concentrated must from the same AOC. That differs from the outright ban for AOGs
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Room for crus
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Crus may be delimited within an AOC under stricter conditions
slides.1.content: A common trap: AOGs ban enrichment, while AOCs may have it in very poor years.
slides.2.title: The three AOCs compared
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Les Coteaux de l'Atlas (1998)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Within Beni-M'Tir. Up to 60 hl/ha, at least 3,000 vines/ha. Minimum alcohol: red 12.5, rosé and gris 12, white 11.5
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Crémant de l'Atlas (2009)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The same area as Coteaux de l'Atlas, traditional-method sparkling wine, with conditions set by the 2008 order on the name "Crémant"
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Les Côtes de Rommani (2014)
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Within Zaër. Hand-picked, vinified the same day, trellis only. Up to 60 hl/ha, at least 3,333 vines/ha. Minimum alcohol: red 13, rosé and gris 12.5, white 12
slides.2.content: The key: Côtes de Rommani is stricter than Coteaux de l'Atlas, half a degree higher and hand-picked.
slides.3.title: Blend rules
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Coteaux de l'Atlas red, rosé, gris
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah and Tempranillo form a group of at least two-thirds, alongside a group of Carignan, Cinsault and Grenache
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Coteaux de l'Atlas white
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Vermentino at least 50%; Ugni Blanc and Clairette at most 50%
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Côtes de Rommani red, rosé, gris
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo, Merlot, Marselan, Tannat and Malbec at least 80%; Carignan, Cinsault and Grenache at most 20%
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Côtes de Rommani white
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Viognier, Vermentino, Colombard and Gros Manseng
slides.3.content: Both AOCs favour international grapes, with traditional ones in support: the reverse of national plantings.
slides.4.title: How many AOCs: three or five?
slides.4.highlights.0.title: The ONSSA page
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Lists three AOCs: Les Coteaux de l'Atlas, Crémant de l'Atlas and Les Côtes de Rommani. This course follows these three
slides.4.highlights.1.title: French Wikipedia
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Adds Côtes de Sebaa Ayoun and Hauts Plateaux de Meknès from 2022, but this course could not locate the orders, so they are not tested
slides.4.highlights.2.title: The right attitude
slides.4.highlights.2.content: State your source and date when answering, for example "three according to ONSSA, with sources reporting two more in 2022"
slides.4.content: Systems change, and a figure you cannot trace should be flagged honestly.
